_about: Hoppaz background music candidates for Jae to audition, ElevenLabs Music. Instrumental only. A Lagos producer makes the final later. Read by the generator script; the key is never in this file.

request.formats_note: Best allowed first. A real 3 s call proved this key accepts pcm_48000 (lossless 48 kHz 16-bit stereo), so raw takes are WAV and the loop step makes the only lossy encode. The free length-validation probe cannot tell formats apart (the length error comes first).
request.note: prompt mode (not composition_plan) because force_instrumental only works with prompt. Seed is not allowed with prompt. Verified live: music_v2_5 and music_v2 both accept 3000 ms and return 44.1 kHz stereo mp3 at 128 kbps, about 0.03 s longer than asked.

loop_rule: Every length is a whole number of bars at the track BPM so the file can be cut on bar lines. Cut the final loop at 8 or 16 bars inside the take, on a downbeat, and crossfade a few ms if needed. Menu tracks are 20 bars, play tracks 24 bars.

cost.measured: 3 s = 38, 10 s = 125, 3 s on music_v2 = 38 (usage-by-model readout). Linear at 12.5 credits per second, same price on music_v2 and music_v2_5. No cost header is returned by /v1/music.

waves.1: One candidate per slot. Run first.
waves.2: Second play_day flavour. Run only if the 675 credits of music spend that predates the probe does not count against the 3000.
waves.3: Reserve. Defined and ready, switched off (enabled false). Turn on only with more budget.

experiments_not_enabled.note: The live API accepts generation_mode track, loop, ambience, video_to_music (checked with a free validation call), but the docs do not mention it. If it yields seamless loops it would beat bar-line cutting. Untested, so not used. A test costs credits at 12.5 per second.

tracks.prompt: Instrumental only: no vocals, no chants, no choir, no spoken voice. Adventurous, bouncy, cheeky overworld theme for a Lagos street-party map game, loud and bright and a little mischievous, not luxe. Modern Afrobeats groove, 2020s Lagos production, 112 BPM, D major, syncopated 3-2 feel. Talking drum and agogo bell trade short call-and-response phrases on top, shekere drives steady sixteenth notes, a warm round bass bounces under a punchy kick and rim-click snare, and bright clean palm-muted highlife guitar plays pentatonic licks between the phrases. A catchy hook on plucked guitar climbs D5, F sharp 5, A5 (short, short, long) and returns every four bars. Steady tempo, exactly 112 BPM in 4/4, no tempo changes. Full groove from the very first beat: no intro build, no riser, no drum roll, no breakdown, no drop, no fade out, no ending, no final hit. The last bar is as full as the first, so it loops cleanly. Consistent energy from start to finish.
